title: Dependency threshold synthesis and safe fallback playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a unified circuit-breaker policy synthesis that computes enforceable trip thresholds across three axes (dependency, model variant, tenant) and ensures deterministic, safe fallback behavior during partial degradations or multi-region failover events. This ticket is the design+implementation playbook: policy math, runtime integration points, rollout plan, and observability/runbook requirements.

Background: We already have ad-hoc breakers on some dependencies and region-level failover, but incidents have shown inconsistent trip behaviors across tenants and model variants leading to client-visible errors or expensive fallbacks (full model swaps) that blow past SLOs. We need a coherent system that: (1) computes trip thresholds considering historical latency/error distributions and SLOs, (2) supports tiered hysteresis (soft-trip, hard-trip, probation), (3) applies policies deterministically in the serving runtime, and (4) routes to precomputed safe fallbacks (lighter model, cached response, or regional replica) with bounded cost and quality regressions.

Scope and non-goals: Scope includes policy synthesis service, runtime enforcement hooks, fallback routing table, feature flags for gradual rollout, dashboards and alerting, and runbook updates. Non-goal: automated model retraining or creating new model variants — the system will only select existing compatible fallbacks.

Acceptance criteria: 
- A policy synthesizer service that emits per-dependency, per-model-variant, and per-tenant thresholds into a consistent, versioned config store.
- Serving runtime can evaluate synthesized policies within request path with <250us median added latency.
- Fallback routing table with prioritized, compatible fallbacks and deterministic selection logic (no random backstop choices).
- Three-step hysteresis implemented: soft-trip (reduce throughput % for tenant), probation window (monitor), hard-trip (fallback routing + shed non-critical traffic).
- End-to-end test harness reproducing a high-error dependency and validating user-visible SLO impact <= defined budget and safe rollback behavior.
- Dashboards showing trip rate, hysteresis state counts, fallback usage, and cost delta per tenant.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
1) Threshold calculation: Use P95 latency and error-rate percentiles per dependency/model/tenant with a small systematic safety margin (configurable multiplier). Advantage: robust to outliers; trade-off: may under-react to sudden increases. We add an adaptive window (combination of 1hr and 5min windows) to detect sudden regressions.
2) Granularity: Primary enforcement is per-dependency and per-model-variant. Tenant-level overrides exist only for high-importance customers (managed via allowlist) to avoid explosion of config volume.
3) Hysteresis: Implement three explicit states (OK, SOFT, HARD) with configurable time windows and step changes in allowed throughput to prevent oscillation.
4) Deterministic fallback selection: Fallback table is generated offline by the synthesizer and includes compatibility metadata (max-sequence, tokenizer, deterministic quality score delta). Routing chooses the highest-priority fallback that keeps cost within configured budget. Deterministic selection avoids audio/video regression in logs and simplifies debugging.
5) Multi-region considerations: Primary preference is regional replica; if regional capacity exhausted or region-wide hard-trip, route to next region using sticky-key affinity when possible. Session-affinity window is configurable and short (e.g., 30s) to limit cross-region churn.

Implementation plan: 
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): Policy synthesizer prototype that reads metric streams and emits thresholds; add config storage (versioned JSON blobs). Unit tests for math.
- Phase 2 (2 sprints): Runtime integration hooks (policy evaluator) + lightweight in-memory cache for threshold configs; implement soft-trip throttling (rate limiter per tenant).
- Phase 3 (2 sprints): Probation/hard-trip and deterministic fallback router; add fallbacks table generator and compatibility checks.
- Phase 4 (1 sprint): Observability, dashboards, runbook, and canary rollout behind feature flag.

Testing and validation: 
- Synthetic fault injection harness to simulate dependency errors/latency at various magnitudes.
- Integration tests validating hysteresis transitions and deterministic fallback selection.
- Load tests verifying <250us median added latency for policy evaluation under 95th percentile QPS.
- Chaos run in staging across multi-region cluster to validate failover correctness and cost bounding.

Rollout and rollback plan: 
- Start behind a feature flag; enable for internal tenants only.
- Canary for 5% of production traffic with a read-only dry-run mode (log decisions, don't enforce).
- Enable enforcement for low-risk tenants first, then escalate to broader cohorts.
- Immediate rollback knob: globally disable synthesized policy enforcement and revert to previous breaker behavior in config store.

Observability & alerts: 
- Dashboards: policy-synth throughput, per-policy trip state counts, fallback-invocations by type, cost delta.
- Alerts: high hard-trip rate across many tenants (page), elevated fallback-cost delta > threshold (page), stuck probation windows (pager), and config synthesis failures (pager).

Runbook summary: 
- If pages triggered for cross-tenant hard-trips, run mitigation: enable global disable, re-route heavy tenants to cached endpoints or increase regional capacity, contact SRE for capacity ramp.
- If false positives: lower sensitivity multiplier, increase probation window, and annotate offending policy for re-synthesis.

Security and data considerations: configs are versioned and stored in KMS-backed store; access controlled via RBAC. Fallback decisions do not alter request payloads and respect PII handling policies.

Open questions: 
- Exact sensitivity multiplier default value (proposal: 1.2 for P95s) and whether to make it per-dependency class.
- Whether to allow automatic tenant-level tuning over time (adaptive learning) or keep manual/operator-driven to avoid unexpected regressions.
- How to account for cost-per-token deltas when comparing model fallback quality vs. expense across heterogeneous hardware.
